Q: How to convert to string an 'allows ref struct' generic argument? A:

The proposal for allos ref struct doesn't explicitly cover how to call object methods.

However, looking at a similar generic method;

public string? Method<T>(T arg) where T : struct
  => arg.ToString();

Results in the IL sequence constrained, callvirt. For the constrained opcode;

If thisType is a value type and thisType does not implement method then ptr is dereferenced, boxed, and passed as the 'this' pointer to the callvirt method instruction

Which is clearly not going to work with a ref struct type.

Instead you could require that all type arguments implement IFormattable;

public string? Method<T>(T arg) where T : IFormattable, allows ref struct
  => arg.ToString(null, CultureInfo.CurrentCulture);

Which should be equivalent to how $"{arg}" would otherwise be compiled. If DefaultInterpolatedStringHandler supported ref struct at least.

Or introduce your own, similar interface, and force all callers to implement it.

Q: How to sum string value in lodash by particular column? A:

Since the values are strings, the + means concatenation, not addition. You can supply a callback to the _.sumBy function:

_.sumBy(data, item => Number(item.extendedPrice));

Working demo:

var data = [{extendedPrice: "5151.059", month: "January"}, 
            {extendedPrice: "8921.0336", month: "March"},
            {extendedPrice: "2036.9865", month: "April"}];

var sumValue = _.sumBy(data, item => Number(item.extendedPrice));
console.log(sumValue);

Q: How to correctly package a n electron app into a Flatpak with a custom app icon and set up file associations? A:

This is a regression likely due to flatpak changing the internal file structure and adding export rules for pixmaps.

Fixing it:
You can get icons to work with flatpak by defining flatpak.icon as an object with each icon size as the key and the asset as the value like so:

"flatpak": {
  . . .
  "icon": {
    "16x16": "dist/icons/16x16.png",
    "32x32": "dist/icons/32x32.png",
    "48x48": "dist/icons/48x48.png",
    "64x64": "dist/icons/64x64.png",
    "128x128": "dist/icons/128x128.png",
    "256x256": "dist/icons/256x256.png",
    "512x512": "dist/icons/512x512.png",
  }
  . . .
}

I'm not sure you can do this while putting the build instructions in the package.json. The project I'm working in uses a forge.config.ts file which can have this hacked in by typing it as unknown instead of string.

Explanation:
The electron flatpak building logic is over 5 years old. At some point, there was a regression introduced where electron-forge passes an icon to @malept/electron-installer-flatpak, and this library puts the icon into /export/share/pixmaps/package.id.path.png. Flatpak does not allow this to export, probably because pixmaps should be .xpm. You can't just pass the icon as a .xpm though, because the underlying library converts it to .png. However, the underlying library also allows icon to be passed as an object with sizes as keys and local path to the icons as the values as above. The underlying library will pass those icons to /export/share/icons, which then work as expected.

Why doesn't the files object work?
The files object copies the files to a /files subdirectory, making them not visible to the /export directory.

Q: C++26 constant_wrapper and constant_arg_t A:

The paper that introduced the name change from nontype to constant_arg has a section 4.4 Replacing std::nontype with std::constant_wrapper :

The seemingly obvious solution is to use std::constant_wrapper from [P2781R9]. The option to use std::constant_­wrapper as a replacement for std::nontype was discussed during an LEWG telecon 2025-03-11.

In short, the problems stem from the fact that std::constant_wrapper is already invocable; it already has a call operator, whose semantics would be ignored by std::function_ref, in a way that is inconsistent with how std::constant_wrapper behaves anywhere else.

More details can be found in [P3740R1], as well as in [P3792R0] "Why constant_wrapper is not a usable replacement for nontype".

In any case, LEWG already decided (with paper-thin consensus) not to pursue this path.

TL;DR: It was considered, but there are reasons to keep the two separate.

Q: IIS express serves one .asmx service, but always returns 404 on another A:

I accidentally created a virtual path that was the same as my asmx path, this prevented the normal asmx handler/path resolution from working. I fixed the problem by opening up C:\Windows\System32\inetsrv\config\applicationHost.config and removing the site with the same name as my asmx file. Dumb and it took me forever to figure it out (seconds to fix of course).
